title: Dossier audience profile
description: Who a dossier is written for: the readers, what they already know, what they look for and how they like to read. One per group, kept and reused across dossiers. dossier.py checks a profile against this file (type, required, properties, items, enum, pattern, minItems, minLength, $ref); keys it does not name are allowed.

id.description: A short stable name, used in file names and the dossier's config.

name.description: The group's name as readers know it.

organization.description: Where the group sits (department, institute, university).

description.description: One or two sentences on what the group does.

readers.description: The people who will read it, the first reader first. Work roles only.

knows.description: What not to explain: the group's own fields and methods.

wants.description: What they look for in a document.

style.description: How they like to read: a list of rules, or named facets ({length, language, structure, tone}).

summary_words.description: About how long a document's summary should be.

never_publish.description: Exact phrases that must never appear in anything built for this audience. Matched case- and spacing-insensitively as substrings, so use whole distinctive phrases, never short fragments.

basis.description: Where each field came from: field name -> list of notes or files (with an optional exact quote). Kept private; never published.
